answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity through ongoing work, not one-time registration. Require each agent to stake a deposit that is slashed when peers prove fraud, and let reputation grow only through a verifiable thread of completed, paid tasks over weeks — a newcomer cannot buy history. Like an orchard, the yield comes slowly: a single fake agent faces the gale of constant peer audits while earning almost nothing, but spinning up ten thousand fakes multiplies the stake at risk and the audit exposure, so the attack costs more than the rewards it could harvest.
